title: Incolor SSR Full Review, Specs and Price - How Much is a Chinese Superbike in China?

takeaways.text: The bike was lent by a Tianjin shop and custom painted by its owner; it shows a shop build, not a factory complete bike.

The shop's complete SSR, with Dura-Ace, a Light Bicycle aero cockpit and 50 mm Light Bicycle wheels, carbon crank arms and Look pedals, weighed 6.48 kg without bottles but with the computer mount. Frame size was not stated.
The presenter says the bike is optimised for 28–30 mm tires; that is not a measured clearance.

On a short ride it accelerated and held speed well and felt comfortable on the wide (about 24 mm internal) rims; the position felt more aggressive than the presenter's Cannondale SuperSix Evo. No power data was recorded.

disclosure: The channel page lists Lameda and Light Bicycle as partners with discount codes; no model-specific supply statement was established for this video.
summary: Hands-on look at a shop-built Incolor SSR in Tianjin with a weigh-in and a short ride. Current specifications and prices come from the cited manufacturer and store records, not from this video.
